slides.title: WHAT IS TRUTH
slides.body: Part III: Why Suffering?
slides.notes: Welcome back. Two nights of evidence; tonight, the message. [IMAGE: series title art, matching Parts I-II]

slides.title: THE SCOREBOARD
slides.notes: Recap briskly. Night 1: relative truth collapsed under real evil; we wrote a five-criteria spec for an absolute moral truth, and you took a wager. Night 2: criterion 2 on trial — Daniel's manuscripts physically predate the fulfillments; the 70 weeks landed on AD 27; an 1838 published calculation named August 1840, and friend and foe alike conceded the event.

slides.title: Five criteria
slides.body:
1. Consistent written record ✓  (5,800+ manuscripts; Dead Sea Scrolls)
2. Above human origins ✓  (the prophecies — tested last night)
3. Practical ✓   4. Universal ✓
5. Benevolent — ?
slides.notes: Four criteria evidenced. One question mark left — and it is the biggest one.

slides.title: The last criterion
slides.body:
Benevolent: does it actually FIX our problem?
Tonight is not more proof THAT the Book is divine.
Tonight is what the divine Book SAYS.
slides.notes: Frame shift: from apologetics to content. The audience earned this night by sitting through the evidence.

slides.body: “For I know the thoughts that I think toward you, saith the LORD, thoughts of peace, and not of evil, to give you an expected end.”
slides.notes: God's stated intent — 'peace, and not of evil.' That is the claim on trial tonight, against everything you have ever suffered.

slides.title: WHY SUFFERING?
slides.notes: The question every worldview must answer — and the reason many of you are not religious. Honor that. [IMAGE: a hospital corridor / empty chair — restrained, not manipulative]

slides.title: The riddle
slides.body:
Is God willing to prevent suffering, but not able? Then He is not all-powerful.
Is He able, but not willing? Then He is not all-good.
Is He both able and willing? Then where does suffering come from?
— traditionally ascribed to Epicurus (via Lactantius, De Ira Dei 13); authorship debated — the challenge stands regardless
slides.notes: Lead with their strongest punch. ATTRIBUTION CARE: it survives only in Lactantius (c. 313 CE); scholars (Glei 1988) doubt Epicurus authored it — the slide says so, which protects you. The whole night answers this riddle: He is willing, He is able, and there is a reason it is not done YET — a reason you can inspect.

slides.title: Two questions for every worldview
slides.body:
1. Where did suffering come from?
2. Does it ever actually END?
Same two questions for every view tonight — including the Bible's.
slides.notes: State the rule ONCE so it doesn't feel rigged. The audience watches whether you score everyone on the same scale — including yourself.

slides.body: “…no design, no purpose, no evil and no good, nothing but blind pitiless indifference.”
slides.extra: — Richard Dawkins, River Out of Eden (1995), ch. 4 — the materialist answer
slides.notes: FAIRNESS: this is the most intellectually honest view in one respect — it refuses to pretend suffering means something. But on its own terms there is no WHY and no END; entropy wins. Diagnosis without cure. DO NOT say atheists have no morals or don't care — they fight suffering hard; it is their metaphysics that offers no remedy, not their character.

slides.title: Buddhism
slides.body:
Suffering (dukkha) arises from craving (tanha); it ends by extinguishing craving — nirvana, via the Eightfold Path.
(Four Noble Truths — the Buddha's first sermon)
slides.notes: FAIRNESS: Buddhism takes BOTH questions seriously — a real explanation and a real path. The honest limitation, stated gently: the cure works by releasing the attachments — the very stuff love is made of; the person is released rather than the world restored. DO NOT call it nihilistic or pessimistic; compassion (karuna) is central. No caricature.

slides.title: Hinduism
slides.body:
Suffering is karma working itself out across many lives (samsara); it ends at moksha — liberation from the cycle.
(Britannica: karma, samsara, moksha)
slides.notes: FAIRNESS: karma is a PRECISE explanation — nothing is random, everything is earned — and moksha is a real end. The honest tension: present suffering reads as deserved (the suffering child is reaping prior-life acts), which many find hard to square with compassion. DO NOT use caste gotchas or 'you had it coming' framing; thoughtful Hindus emphasize reducing others' suffering as itself dharma.

slides.title: Islam
slides.body: Suffering is a test (ibtila) within God's decree — “He created death and life to test you, which of you is best in deed” (Qur'an 67:2) — with full justice in the hereafter.
slides.notes: FAIRNESS: Islam answers BOTH questions — a meaningful test under a wise God, and paradise with perfect justice. The honest point: the resolution is deferred entirely to the next life, and on WHY God decrees this specific suffering the tradition counsels reverent silence (Qur'an 21:23). DO NOT call Islam fatalistic — mainstream Sunni theology affirms human responsibility alongside qadar.

slides.title: New Age
slides.body: Suffering is illusion or self-generated — ego, resistance, “the pain-body” (Tolle, The Power of Now) — and dissolves through awakened consciousness.
slides.notes: FAIRNESS: the perception point is partly true — much suffering IS amplified by the mind, and presence-practices bring real relief. The documented critique (state it as critics state it, never as mockery): applied to a child's starvation, genocide, or trauma, 'illusion / you attracted it' becomes victim-blaming — the framework must deny the suffering is real or blame the sufferer. No cheap 'vibrations' laugh line — it alienates the seekers in the room.

slides.body: “O LORD, how long shall I cry, and thou wilt not hear! … Why dost thou shew me iniquity, and cause me to behold grievance?”
slides.extra: — Habakkuk 1:2-3 (KJV) — the Bible asks the question first
slides.notes: Before the Bible answers the question, it ASKS it — rawer than most skeptics dare: Job 30:26 ('when I looked for good, then evil came'); Eccl 4:1 ('the tears of such as were oppressed… no comforter'). The Book does not dodge. That alone separates it from the sales brochures.

slides.title: A different shape of answer
slides.body:
Suffering is an INTRUDER — not original, not illusion, not deserved, not forever.
And it will be ABOLISHED: the person kept, the world restored,
guaranteed by Someone outside the system.
slides.notes: State it humbly — a claim to be weighed, not a trump card. Every view above either explains origin without a guaranteed external END, or offers escape that dissolves the self, defers wholly to an afterlife, or denies the suffering is real. The Bible's answer is a different SHAPE. Now weigh it.

slides.title: THE ANSWER BEGINS: LOVE
slides.notes: Everything that follows must stay consistent with one axiom — or the story fails on its own terms.

slides.body: “He that loveth not knoweth not God; for God is love.”
slides.notes: Not 'God loves' — God IS love (also 1 John 4:16). His essence. Hold every move tonight against this axiom; that is the test the Book invites.

slides.title: Love cannot be compelled
slides.body:
A forced “I love you” is not love.
Love requires freedom.
Freedom creates risk.
slides.notes: Three lines, slowly. This is the hinge of the whole theodicy. (EGW shaping, notes only: 'God takes no pleasure in a forced obedience; and to all He grants freedom of will' — PP 34.3.) [IMAGE: open hands / unlocked door]

slides.body: “I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life…”
slides.notes: God stacks the appeal — 'therefore choose LIFE' — and still leaves the choice. He argues; He does not seize.

slides.body: “…choose you this day whom ye will serve… but as for me and my house, we will serve the LORD.”
slides.notes: Allegiance invited, never coerced — modeled at the highest level of the Book's own story.

slides.title: Made free
slides.body:
“So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him…” — Genesis 1:27
Image of God = moral agency. Not automation.
slides.notes: The image (Gen 1:26-27) grounds the capacity for genuine choice that love requires. Robots cannot love; that is the point of not making robots.

slides.body: “Come now, and let us reason together, saith the LORD…”
slides.notes: God's recruiting method: reason. Mark this verse — it returns at the end of the night.

slides.title: The risk of freedom
slides.body:
If creatures can truly choose love,
they can truly refuse it.
The question was never IF freedom would be tested — but what God would do when it was.
slides.notes: Pivot line into the rebellion. Pause before advancing.

slides.title: THE REBELLION
slides.notes: [IMAGE: storm / fractured light — abstract, no horns-and-pitchfork kitsch]

slides.body: “And there was war in heaven: Michael and his angels fought against the dragon… And the great dragon was cast out, that old serpent, called the Devil, and Satan, which deceiveth the whole world…”
slides.notes: THE ANCHOR TEXT — explicit, names 'the Devil, and Satan' directly; no interpretive caveat needed. Lead the origin-of-evil case here (v2 audit decision), and let Ezekiel 28 / Isaiah 14 be illustrative.

slides.title: Where evil began
slides.body:
“Thou wast perfect in thy ways from the day that thou wast created, till iniquity was found in thee.” — Ezekiel 28:15
(spoken of the king of Tyre — long read as describing the power behind the throne)
slides.notes: HONESTY ON SLIDE (v2 audit): the surface addressee is the king of Tyrus; the Lucifer application is the traditional dual-fulfillment reading — and v13 ('thou hast been in Eden… the anointed cherub,' v14) is why readers for centuries saw more than a Phoenician king here. The point that matters: evil began in the HIGHEST created being — perfect until self-corrupted — so it cannot be blamed on a design flaw.

slides.title: The five “I wills”
slides.body:
“…I will ascend into heaven, I will exalt my throne above the stars of God… I will be like the most High.” — Isaiah 14:13-14
(a taunt against Babylon's king — the same pattern of self-exaltation)
slides.notes: Same honest handling: context is the king of Babylon (Isa 14:4); 'Lucifer' renders Hebrew helel, 'morning star.' The pattern is the point: not a grievance — an ambition. 'I will be LIKE the most High': not love seeking to serve, but self seeking the throne.

slides.title: A war of words, not weapons
slides.body:
“…He was a murderer from the beginning, and abode not in the truth… he is a liar, and the father of it.” — John 8:44
The rebellion's weapon was never force. It was DECEPTION.
slides.notes: Jesus' own verdict. A lie about WHAT? About God — about what kind of ruler He is. Which is why the conflict cannot be settled by force: lies are not killed with swords.

slides.body: “…for the accuser of our brethren is cast down, which accused them before our God day and night.”
slides.notes: Scripture's own title for the enemy: THE ACCUSER. Pivot the room: this is a courtroom, not a battlefield. (Zech 3:1-2 — a second courtroom scene, Satan 'standing to resist' a believer.)

slides.title: The accusation
slides.body:
1. God is selfish and tyrannical.
2. His law is arbitrary — impossible to keep.
3. He buys loyalty: worship is bribery.
4. He is unjust and vengeful.
slides.notes: Name the charges — a vague 'problem of evil' cannot be answered; a specific indictment can. Receipts: #1 Gen 3:5 ('God doth know…' — He's holding out on you); #2 the serpent's first move, 'Hath God said?'; #3 Job 1:9-11 (next slide); #4 the caricature every skeptic carries. The rest of the night answers each one with evidence.

slides.title: A courtroom, not a battlefield
slides.body:
The universe — the watching jury (“we are made a spectacle… to angels, and to men,” 1 Cor 4:9)
Earth — the exhibit
Satan — the prosecutor (Rev 12:10)
God — the accused
slides.notes: The classroom analogy (the user's own move, LGT-1): a student stands up and claims the teacher's rules are unfair — and the whole class watches BOTH the claim and the evidence. Expelling the student doesn't answer the claim. [IMAGE: empty courtroom]

slides.body: “Doth Job fear God for nought? … But put forth thine hand now, and touch all that he hath, and he will curse thee to thy face.”
slides.notes: Charge #3 live: loyalty is bought — 'hast not thou made an hedge about him?' The only way to DISPROVE 'they serve you because it pays' is to let the hedge down. There is no third option; that is the terrible logic of the trial.

slides.title: Watch who does the striking
slides.body:
“So went Satan forth from the presence of the LORD, and smote Job with sore boils…” — Job 2:7
God permits. The accuser afflicts.
slides.notes: CRITICAL HANDLING (v2 audit): Job himself, in his grief, says 'the LORD hath taken away' (Job 1:21) — but the narration tells us who actually struck (Job 2:7). Always pair them, or the deck teaches the opposite of its own thesis. Job's faith is the right response; the narrator's camera is the right theology.

slides.title: WHY NOT JUST DESTROY HIM?
slides.notes: The question everyone is now asking. Good — it means they accepted the frame.

slides.title: You cannot execute an accusation
slides.body:
Kill the accuser — the accusation survives, whispered forever.
A defendant who destroys his accuser looks guilty.
A defendant who answers with evidence wins in the open.
slides.notes: The user's signature one-liners (Way Home pt 1) — plain courtroom logic, no theology needed yet. Let it land as common sense.

slides.title: Force ≠ vindication
slides.body:
If God had destroyed Lucifer on the spot,
the watching universe would have served Him from FEAR —
and fear is exactly what the accusation claimed His government ran on.
The charge would have been proven by the rebuttal.
slides.notes: (EGW shaping, notes only — GC 498.3: 'Had he been immediately blotted from existence, they would have served God from fear rather than from love… Evil must be permitted to come to maturity.') On the slide it stands as plain logic; it needs no authority.

slides.body: “…let God be true, but every man a liar; as it is written, That thou mightest be justified in thy sayings, and mightest overcome when thou art judged.”
slides.notes: THE CENTRAL VERSE OF THE NIGHT. God consents to BE JUDGED — and to win by evidence, not by silencing the court. (Interpretive note: Paul is quoting Ps 51:4 on God's faithfulness; the 'God submits to judgment' application is defensible and the KJV wording carries it — use it knowingly.) Everything in this series — testable prophecy, public fulfillment, the invitation to verify — is this verse in action.

slides.body: “…we are made a spectacle unto the world, and to angels, and to men.”
slides.notes: The audience is real (also Eph 3:10 — God's wisdom made known 'unto the principalities and powers in heavenly places' through events down here). The trial is public because the verdict must hold for every onlooker, forever.

slides.title: So the claims must be tested
slides.body:
Evil must be allowed to show what it IS —
so the verdict, when it comes, stands forever. Beyond all question.
slides.notes: (EGW shaping, notes only — GC 499.1: the rebellion's history becomes 'a perpetual safeguard to all holy intelligences.') The cost of a permanent answer is letting the experiment run. That cost is the world you live in — which is where we go next.

slides.title: THE TEST COMES TO EARTH
slides.notes: [IMAGE: garden / fruit — restrained]

slides.title: One tree
slides.body: “Of every tree of the garden thou mayest FREELY eat: but of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, thou shalt not eat of it: for in the day that thou eatest thereof thou shalt surely die.” — Genesis 2:16-17
slides.notes: Total freedom — 'of EVERY tree, freely' — one test, stakes stated in advance. Not a minefield; a single fence, labeled.

slides.title: The same lie, retold
slides.body:
“Ye shall not surely die: for God doth know that in the day ye eat thereof… ye shall be as gods…” — Genesis 3:4-5
The accusation, repackaged for humans: God is holding out on you.
slides.notes: Connect it explicitly: the serpent's pitch IS charge #1 from the courtroom slide — God is selfish; His rules protect His privilege, not you. Same prosecutor, new jury.

slides.title: Humanity switched sides
slides.body:
“…she took of the fruit thereof, and did eat, and gave also unto her husband with her; and he did eat.” — Genesis 3:6
We believed the accuser. And the dominion of this world changed hands.
slides.notes: Don't moralize the fruit; the issue is allegiance — whose word about God did humanity trust? The answer rearranged the planet.

slides.body: “All this power will I give thee, and the glory of them: for that is delivered unto me; and to whomsoever I will I give it.”
slides.extra: — Luke 4:5-6 (KJV) — the devil's claim. Jesus did not dispute it.
slides.notes: Satan claims the world's kingdoms were 'DELIVERED' to him — and Jesus, who contradicts liars for a living, lets the claim stand. John 12:31 next: Jesus' own title for him.

slides.body: “Now is the judgment of this world: now shall the prince of this world be cast out.”
slides.notes: 'The PRINCE of this world' — Jesus' own label for Satan. Note the verse for later: it is a CROSS saying (callback in §8). The world you see is under hostile management.

slides.title: The wages
slides.body:
“Wherefore, as by one man sin entered into the world, and death by sin; and so death passed upon all men…” — Romans 5:12
“For the wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life…” — Romans 6:23
slides.notes: Death is an ENTRANT — 'sin ENTERED… and death BY sin' — not part of the original design. Gen 3:17-19 in the same breath: thorns, toil, decay — the broken economy of a cursed ground. And Rom 6:23 already smuggles in the rescue: 'but the GIFT.'

slides.title: So whose world is this?
slides.body:
The broken world you see is NOT the world God made.
It is the rebellion's exhibit — running its course in front of the watching universe.
slides.notes: This reframe answers half the riddle from §2: the suffering you indict God for is the evidence-in-progress AGAINST the accuser. (2 Cor 4:4 — 'the god of this world hath blinded the minds' — even our seeing is contested ground; say it gently.)

slides.title: WHY SUFFERING, THEN?
slides.notes: Now the mechanics — four honest pieces: harvest, hostile author, entanglement, and a God who climbs into it.

slides.title: Harvest, not punishment
slides.body:
“Be not deceived; God is not mocked: for whatsoever a man soweth, that shall he also reap.” — Galatians 6:7
“They have sown the wind, and they shall reap the whirlwind.” — Hosea 8:7
slides.notes: Much suffering is CONSEQUENCE in a moral universe — compounding like interest (wind in, whirlwind out) — not lightning bolts from an offended deity. James 1:13-15 next makes the exoneration explicit.

slides.body: “Let no man say when he is tempted, I am tempted of God: for God cannot be tempted with evil, neither tempteth he any man… Then when lust hath conceived, it bringeth forth sin: and sin, when it is finished, bringeth forth death.”
slides.notes: The chain runs desire → sin → death — internal to the human, explicitly NOT authored by God. The Book exonerates God of the very thing the riddle charges Him with.

slides.title: “An enemy hath done this”
slides.body:
A man sowed good seed in his field — but while men slept, his enemy came and sowed tares among the wheat.
“He said unto them, An enemy hath done this.” — Matthew 13:24-28
slides.notes: Jesus' own theodicy parable. The field's owner did not plant the tares. Suffering has a HOSTILE AUTHOR — the third honest piece. [IMAGE: wheat field]

slides.title: Then why not rip it out NOW?
slides.body: “Wilt thou then that we go and gather them up? But he said, Nay; lest while ye gather up the tares, ye root up also the wheat with them. Let both grow together until the harvest.” — Matthew 13:28-30
slides.notes: The servants ask the skeptic's exact question. The answer: every life is entangled with every other — a surgical strike on evil harvests the innocent with it (which abuser is also a father? which corrupt system also feeds people?). The only CLEAN end is at the harvest — which is scheduled (§10).

slides.body: “For he doth not afflict willingly nor grieve the children of men.”
slides.notes: Written from inside a national catastrophe (Jerusalem's ruins) — not from a podium. The explicit divine disposition: affliction is not His delight.

slides.body: “In all their affliction he was afflicted… in his love and in his pity he redeemed them; and he bare them, and carried them all the days of old.”
slides.notes: Not a spectator God. 'In all THEIR affliction HE was afflicted' — He suffers WITH. The next two slides sharpen it to a point.

slides.body: “Jesus wept.”
slides.extra: — John 11:35 (KJV) — the shortest verse in the Bible
slides.notes: At a graveside He was about to EMPTY — He still wept. Grief is not unbelief; God incarnate did it. Let this slide breathe; say almost nothing.

slides.title: Not the armchair deity
slides.body:
“For we have not an high priest which cannot be touched with the feeling of our infirmities; but was in all points tempted like as we are…” — Hebrews 4:15
Whatever else you say about the Bible's God — He did not stay out of the pain.
slides.notes: He has felt it from the inside: hunger, betrayal, injustice, torture, death. That is unique among the §2 answers — and it sets up the cross.

slides.title: THE ANSWER: THE CROSS
slides.notes: [IMAGE: cross silhouette — restrained] The trial's decisive exhibit.

slides.title: The prosecutor's sharpest charge
slides.body:
If the law is just, the lawbreaker cannot be pardoned.
Justice and mercy cannot coexist.
Pick one, God.
slides.notes: (EGW shaping, notes only — DA 761.4: Satan 'declared… that justice was inconsistent with mercy… God could not be just, he urged, and yet show mercy to the sinner.') The dilemma is real — every human court faces it. The cross is the only answer that takes BOTH horns.

slides.body: “But God commendeth his love toward us, in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us.”
slides.notes: Love demonstrated 'while we were yet sinners' — BEFORE any merit, for enemies. Evidence, not sentiment.

slides.body: “For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son… For God sent not his Son into the world to condemn the world; but that the world through him might be saved.”
slides.notes: Verse 17 corrects the caricature most skeptics carry: the mission is RESCUE, not condemnation.

slides.title: He did not waive the law — He absorbed it
slides.body:
He did not change the rules to excuse us.
He paid them. Himself.
“God was in Christ, reconciling the world unto himself.” — 2 Corinthians 5:19
slides.notes: (EGW shaping, notes only — DA 762.1: 'God did not change His law, but He sacrificed Himself, in Christ, for man's redemption.') Justice satisfied AND mercy extended — both horns taken at once. The charge of §8's opening slide collapses.

slides.body: “But he was wounded for our transgressions, he was bruised for our iniquities… and with his stripes we are healed… and the LORD hath laid on him the iniquity of us all.”
slides.extra: — Isaiah 53:5-6 (KJV) — written ~7 centuries early; preserved in the Great Isaiah Scroll, copied ~125 BC — before the event
slides.notes: HERE the Great Isaiah Scroll argument is VALID (v2 audit): the scroll (~125 BC) physically predates the crucifixion (AD 31) — unlike the Cyrus case, where it postdates the fulfillment. The substitution chapter was on parchment in a cave at Qumran while Rome was still a republic. Last night's method, applied to tonight's centerpiece.

slides.title: The accuser unmasked
slides.body:
At the cross the watching universe saw the accuser torture and kill the only innocent man.
Whatever sympathy his case still had — died there.
“…having spoiled principalities and powers, he made a shew of them OPENLY…” — Colossians 2:15
slides.notes: (EGW shaping, notes only — DA 761.2: 'He had revealed himself as a murderer… The last link of sympathy between Satan and the heavenly world was broken.') The prosecutor, given a free hand, produced Calvary — and the jury saw it. His OWN work condemned him.

slides.body: “Blotting out the handwriting of ordinances that was against us… nailing it to his cross; and having spoiled principalities and powers, he made a shew of them openly, triumphing over them in it.”
slides.notes: Two things at once: the legal charge against US is cancelled ('nailed to his cross'), and the powers behind the accusation are publicly exposed. Courtroom language throughout — Paul saw the same trial.

slides.body: “Now is the judgment of this world: now shall the prince of this world be cast out. And I, if I be lifted up from the earth, will draw all men unto me.”
slides.extra: — John 12:31-32 (KJV) — spoken days before the cross
slides.notes: Callback to §6: the 'prince of this world' verse was always a CROSS verse. The casting-out happens at the lifting-up. (1 John 3:8 — 'for this purpose the Son of God was manifested, that he might destroy the works of the devil'; Heb 2:14 — through DEATH he destroys him that had the power of death.)

slides.title: Greater love
slides.body:
“Greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends.” — John 15:13
He would rather die than lose you.
That is criterion 5 — answered in blood.
slides.notes: The benevolence criterion gets its verdict here, not at the end — the scorecard later just records it. Pause. [IMAGE: none — keep stark]

slides.title: THEN WHY IS IT STILL RUNNING?
slides.notes: The honest follow-up: if the cross settled it, why am I still burying people?

slides.body: “The Lord is not slack concerning his promise, as some men count slackness; but is longsuffering to us-ward, not willing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance.”
slides.notes: The delay reframed: not absence, not impotence — mercy with a clock. Every extra day is somebody's rescue window. Maybe yours; that's why you're hearing this.

slides.title: The delay is a rescue window
slides.body: “And this gospel of the kingdom shall be preached in all the world for a witness unto all nations; and THEN shall the end come.” — Matthew 24:14
slides.notes: A stated purpose and a defined endpoint — the timeline is mission-driven, not stalled. The harvest of §7 has a date.

slides.body: “How long, O Lord, holy and true, dost thou not judge and avenge our blood…? And it was said unto them, that they should rest yet for a little season…”
slides.notes: Scripture validates the impatience — the Book's own heroes ask the skeptic's question — and gives the reason for the wait. The Book keeps owning the hard questions; that is its pattern.

slides.body: “For the vision is yet for an appointed time, but at the end it shall speak, and not lie: though it tarry, wait for it; because it will surely come, it will not tarry.”
slides.notes: The same prophet who opened §2 crying 'how long?' receives this answer — APPOINTED time, certain arrival. The loop closes. And after two nights of dated, fulfilled prophecy, 'appointed time' is not a brush-off; it has a track record.

slides.title: HOW IT ENDS
slides.notes: [IMAGE: sunrise — restrained]

slides.body: “Let not your heart be troubled… I go to prepare a place for you. And if I go and prepare a place for you, I will come again, and receive you unto myself; that where I am, there ye may be also.”
slides.notes: The promise in His own words — personal: 'I will come again… receive YOU.'

slides.body: “…this same Jesus, which is taken up from you into heaven, shall so come in like manner as ye have seen him go into heaven.”
slides.notes: Literal and visible — 'in like manner as ye have SEEN him go' — eyewitness-anchored; no spiritualized escape hatch.

slides.body: “For the Lord himself shall descend from heaven with a shout… and the dead in Christ shall rise first: then we which are alive and remain shall be caught up together with them… and so shall we ever be with the Lord.”
slides.notes: Answers the grief in the room: the dead are not lost — they rise FIRST. Reunion is the mechanic of the return.

slides.title: A transparent verdict
slides.body: “And I saw the dead, small and great, stand before God; and the books were opened… and the dead were judged out of those things which were written in the books, according to their works.” — Revelation 20:12
slides.notes: The judgment is evidence-based, recorded, PUBLIC — 'the books were opened.' God ends the case the way He ran it: in the open. (EGW shaping, notes only — GC 666-671: every question answered before the assembled universe; even the accuser concedes the verdict.) This vindicates §5's thesis — He said 'judge me,' and the final scene is exactly that.

slides.body: “…he will make an utter end: affliction shall not rise up the second time.”
slides.notes: The recurrence question — 'won't this just happen again?' — answered: NO. Why not? Because the question was answered in PUBLIC, once, before the whole universe. Destruction at the START would have planted fear; extermination at the END vindicates love — the same act means opposite things before and after the evidence is in. (EGW shaping, notes only — GC 504.1; DA 26.2: 'Rebellion can never again arise… By love's self-sacrifice, the inhabitants of earth and heaven are bound to their Creator in bonds of indissoluble union.')

slides.body: “And God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes; and there shall be no more death, neither sorrow, nor crying, neither shall there be any more pain: for the former things are passed away.”
slides.notes: The payoff verse of the whole night. The tears of Ecclesiastes 4:1 — 'and they had no comforter' — wiped away PERSONALLY. Read it slowly; this is the verse the room came for, whether they know it or not.

slides.title: No more curse
slides.body:
“And there shall be no more curse… and they shall see his face… and there shall be no night there.” — Revelation 22:3-5
The tree of life. His face. Eden — bookended.
slides.notes: Rev 22:1-5: the river, the tree of life, 'the leaves… for the healing of the nations.' Genesis 3's curse is explicitly reversed — the story is a ring, and it closes.

slides.title: A real, physical future
slides.body:
“They shall build houses, and inhabit them; and they shall plant vineyards, and eat the fruit of them… they shall not labour in vain… The wolf and the lamb shall feed together.” — Isaiah 65:21-25
Not clouds and harps. A restored EARTH.
slides.notes: Isa 65:17, 21-25 — houses, vineyards, work that isn't futile (the exact reversal of Gen 3:17-19's cursed toil), predator and prey at peace. Tangible hope for people allergic to vaporous heaven-talk.

slides.body: “Eye hath not seen, nor ear heard, neither have entered into the heart of man, the things which God hath prepared for them that love him.”
slides.notes: Humility cap: everything just shown is the FLOOR, not the ceiling.

slides.title: The two questions, answered
slides.body:
Where did suffering come from?
An intruder — a real rebellion, a real fall.
Does it ever END?
Abolished — person kept, world restored, guaranteed from outside the system.
slides.notes: Hold the Bible's answer to the same two-question scale from §2 — out loud. It is the only answer on tonight's board that scores both, without dissolving the person, deferring everything, or denying the pain.

slides.title: THE VERDICT
slides.notes: Bring the series home.

slides.title: The scorecard
slides.body:
1. Consistent written record ✓
2. Above human origins ✓
3. Practical ✓
4. Universal ✓
5. Benevolent ✓ — it explains the wound, it entered the wound, it ends the wound.
slides.notes: Read line 5 exactly as written — it is the night in one sentence.

slides.title: Three nights ago, you took a wager
slides.body:
If a source met all five — would you follow it?
You said yes.
The evidence is in. The next move is yours.
slides.notes: And notice WHO won't force the move: the God of this Book runs the cosmos by evidence, and He recruits the same way. (EGW shaping, notes only — SC 105.2: 'God never asks us to believe, without giving sufficient evidence… Our faith must rest upon evidence, not demonstration. Those who wish to doubt will have opportunity; while those who really desire to know the truth will find plenty of evidence.') Doubt remains POSSIBLE on purpose — that is what freedom costs, and what love requires. Same logic as §5.

slides.body: “These were more noble… in that they received the word with all readiness of mind, and searched the scriptures daily, whether those things were so.”
slides.extra: — Acts 17:11 (KJV) — the Bereans, commended for fact-checking the preacher
slides.notes: THE verse for this room: the Bible calls people NOBLE for verifying the preacher against the text. Don't take my word for any of this — check me. (John 5:39 — 'Search the scriptures' — it's a command, not a concession.)

slides.body: “Behold, I stand at the door, and knock: if any man hear my voice, and open the door, I will come in to him, and will sup with him, and he with me.”
slides.notes: He knocks. He does not break in. The door handle is on your side — consistent to the last page with everything tonight argued. [IMAGE: door, light under it — restrained]

slides.title: Your move
slides.body:
Study with me — one hour, your questions, any week night.
Or start alone: the Gospel of John, one chapter a night.
Test it the way we tested everything these three nights.
“O taste and see that the LORD is good.” — Psalm 34:8
slides.notes: The ask, both lanes: contact (study together — have a signup sheet or your number ready) and zero-pressure (read John alone). Close on Ps 34:8 — the Book's own empirical challenge, the same verse that opened the night. Prayer if the room allows; otherwise a warm thank-you and availability.
